yq: -P/write-form path still drops one of a floated+own comment collision (#1085's DOM-path half)

## Summary

#1085 fixed the "a floated anchor comment and a target node's own genuine comment can't
coexist" collision for the streaming/get-form path (`succinctly yq '.'`). The DOM path
(`-P`, and every write form: `=`, `|=`, `+=`, `del()`, ...) still shows only one of the two,
because it's a separate code path (`to_owned_with_comments` → `CommentTree`/
`NodeMeta { comment: Option<String>, .. }` in `src/jq/eval_generic.rs` and
`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`), not the streaming cursor path in `src/yaml/light.rs`
that #1085 fixed.

```
$ printf 'a: &anc # deferred comment\n  b: # b own comment\n    c: 1\n' | yq -P '.'
a: &anc
  b: # deferred comment
  # b own comment
    c: 1
$ printf 'a: &anc # deferred comment\n  b: # b own comment\n    c: 1\n' | succinctly yq -P '.'
a: &anc
  b: # deferred comment
    c: 1
```

(Confirmed live against pinned yq v4.53.3.)

## Note: the specific single comment shown has changed since #1085

Before #1085, `-P` showed the key's own comment (`# b own comment`) and dropped the
floated one, because the parser's single `Option` slot kept whichever writer ran first
(`maybe_capture_line_comment`, the key's own capture). #1085 widened that slot to a `Vec`
and swapped the capture order (floated first, then own) so the *streaming* renderer could
emit both in the right order. The DOM path's `to_owned_with_comments` still reads only the
first entry of that `Vec` (via the existing singular `line_comment_raw()` accessor, which
now returns the *first* pushed entry) to seed `NodeMeta.comment`, so it now shows the
*floated* comment (`# deferred comment`) instead and drops the key's own — the opposite
single comment from before, not a fix. Neither shape was pinned by an existing test (the
full `yq_cli_tests.rs`/`yq_golden_tests.rs` suite passed unchanged through #1085's PR), so
this isn't a regression against any prior guarantee, just the pre-existing DOM-path gap
manifesting slightly differently now.

## Root cause / scope

`NodeMeta.comment: Option<String>` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) is a single-slot structure
matching the *old* `NodeComments.line: Option<(u32,u32)>` shape #1085 moved away from at the
parser layer. Making it multi-valued (or joining both entries into one `\n`-embedded string,
mirroring how the still-unimplemented `head`/`foot` write side is meant to work per #798's
closing notes) is a distinct, separate piece of work from #1085's parser/streaming-renderer
fix:

- A different struct (`NodeMeta`, not `SemiIndex::comments`/`NodeComments`).
- A different renderer: `src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`'s DOM emitter (see
  `trailing_comment_suffix`/`append_own_comment_line`, which already implement a
  "first entry inline, rest as standalone lines at indent" split — but currently only for
  one *string* split on embedded `\n` characters coming from a `line_comment =` write, not
  for two independently-captured comments merged from the parse side).
- The seed point from the live cursor into `NodeMeta.comment` at
  `to_owned_with_comments` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`, ~1367-1401 and ~1445) would need to
  consume `YamlCursor::line_comments()` (the new #1085 multi-accessor) instead of the
  singular `line_comment_raw()`, and join or otherwise carry more than one comment through.

This is exactly the kind of split #798 itself went through (spinning off #2795/#2796/#2763
rather than trying to land everything in one PR) — #1085's own investigation and repro only
ever used the streaming path (`succinctly yq '.'`, no `-P` or write forms), so this DOM-path
half was out of its scope.

## Reference

- #1085 (fixed half: streaming/get-form path)
- `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`, "comment placement" list
